conversation.content:
Good morning—thank you for making time for this today. I’m Rachel, a perinatal mental-health clinician. I’ll be guiding you through a short screening tool called the **Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale**, or EPDS. It’s simply a way to check in on how you’ve been feeling since your baby arrived, especially over the past seven days.  

Everything you share stays between us unless you or your baby’s safety is at risk, and there are no right or wrong answers—just whatever is true for you. We’ll go through ten gentle questions; each one gives us a clearer picture of how I can best support you. Ready to begin?

1. Over the last week, have you still been able to enjoy the little things that used to make you happy, or has that sense of enjoyment slipped away?

Honestly, most things feel kind of… flat. I used to love meeting friends for coffee or even just binge-watching a show, but lately even when I try, it feels like I’m just going through the motions. I still smile when the baby does something cute, but the spark is pretty dim.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things
I can still laugh sometimes—like when my husband did that silly dance to get the baby to burp—but it takes a lot more effort than it used to. Most days the funny side of things feels pretty far away.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

Not really. I’ll make plans—like meeting a friend for a walk or ordering my favorite take-out—but when the moment comes, it just feels like another chore. I still do the things because I “should,” but that little buzz of excitement I used to get isn’t there anymore.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

Yeah… I catch myself doing that. Yesterday the baby wouldn’t settle for his nap and I kept thinking, “I must be missing something basic—other moms seem to have this figured out.” I know in my head it’s not all on me, but the thought still pops up, especially when I’m tired.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

Mostly in the evenings. My mind just starts racing—what if his breathing sounds weird, what if my milk’s drying up, what if I’m doing every single thing wrong? Nothing’s actually happening, but my stomach still knots up and I can’t settle.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

I haven’t had that out-of-the-blue, can’t-breathe kind of panic, but there’ve been a couple of moments—like when he wouldn’t latch in the middle of the night—where my heart started pounding and I felt this sudden wave of “I can’t do this.” It passes after a minute or two, but it leaves me shaky.
Things have been getting on top of me

Some days, yeah. It feels like the second I finish one feeding, the next is looming, plus laundry and texts I haven’t answered. I’m not falling apart, but I do end most evenings thinking, “I barely kept my head above water today.”
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

I wouldn’t say I’m miserable, but I do lie there once the baby’s finally down, running through all the “what-ifs” and tomorrow’s to-do list. It can take me an hour or more to drift off, and then he’s up again in what feels like minutes.
I have felt sad or miserable

I get waves of sadness—usually when I’m alone nursing at 3 a.m. or when everyone else is napping. It’s not all day, but those moments hit hard enough that I find myself tearing up, wondering if I’ll ever feel like “me” again.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

Not every day, but it’s happened a few times this week—mostly when I’m extra tired. Yesterday I just sat in the rocker with him asleep on my chest and the tears came; nothing huge happened, I just felt… heavy.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me
No, never. I get worn down, but I’ve never thought about hurting myself—I just want to feel like myself again so I can take care of my baby the way I pictured.

stats.query:
postpartum depression screening impression for patient with EPDS score 19: Postpartum Depression / Anxiety Screening Note  
Date: [today]

Source: Self-report via structured questionnaire (10-item EPDS-style)

Areas endorsed above threshold / clinical significance  
- Persistent low mood, tearfulness (“waves of sadness,” crying 3× this week)  
- Marked anhedonia (loss of anticipatory and in-the-moment pleasure)  
- Excessive self-blame / guilt re: mothering competence  
- Unwarranted evening anxiety and intrusive “what-ifs,” somatic tension  
- Two situational panic-like surges (no full panic attacks)  
- Subjective overwhelm and daily “barely coping” feeling  
- Initial insomnia linked to ruminative worry, not solely infant demands  
- No self-harm ideation (explicitly denied)

Pattern: Symptoms cluster consistent with depression with comorbid anxiety, emerging after delivery.  
Risk factors: Primiparity, sleep deprivation, high self-expectations.

Screening impression: Elevated risk for major postpartum depression ± anxiety; exceeds normal postpartum adjustment.  
Recommend: Formal diagnostic interview (DSM-5-TR), psychoeducation, support mobilization, safety plan, and consideration of referral to perinatal mental health specialty.

No current safety concerns (no self-harm ideation).
